{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a whitespace-padded manifest id is validated trimmed but installed untrimmed**

`WidgetPayloadValidation.id` returns the **raw** `manifest['id']` (untrimmed), while `_checkSchema` validates the **trimmed** form (`rawId.trim()` → `_checkId`) and `WidgetManifest.fromJson` also trims. So a manifest like:

```json
{"id": " fa-agents ", "name": "X", "version": "1.0.0"}
```

passes validation (the id rule `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` is enforced on the trimmed value), and then this line installs it into a **space-padded folder**:

```dart
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: id, // " fa-agents " — written as apps/ fa-agents /manifest.json
  ...
```

Verified locally: `inspection.id` = `" fa-agents "` and the env ends up with `apps/ fa-agents /` + a `.installed.json` key `" fa-agents "` — the stored id violates the very rule the validator just enforced. No traversal risk (regex rejects `/` and `..`), but the widget's stored id no longer matches the id rule, and the folder name carries whitespace everywhere (grid key, `open_app`, records).

Fix (one line, in `UnpackedWidgetLoader.install`):

```dart
final trimmed = id.trim();
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: trimmed,
  version: inspection.version ?? '0.0.0',
  files: inspection.files,
  origin: origin,
);
```

—or reject ids where `id != id.trim()` in the validator with a named `id_invalid` error. A regression test with a padded id belongs in `unpacked_loader_test.dart`.
"}

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the replace warning is skipped for agent-created apps — their code is overwritten silently**

The replace check keys off the install record:

```dart
final replaced = existing.where((app) => app.id == inspection.id).toList();
final existingApp = replaced.isEmpty ? null : replaced.first;
...
existingSource: existingApp?.installSource, // null for agent-created apps
```

and the dialog decides `final replaces = existingSource != null;`.

An **agent-created** app (built with Fa via file tools) has **no** `.installed.json` record, so `installSource` is `null` → `replaces` is `false` → the dialog renders as a plain fresh-load confirm ("Load" button, no warning banner), even though confirming **overwrites that app's code** (`installWidget` only protects files whose hashes are recorded — an agent-created app has none, so every file is replaced; only `storage.json` survives).

Ticket AC4 says "replacing an existing id asks for confirmation" — the load confirm still appears, but the explicit replace warning (naming what is being replaced) fires only when the old install came from the catalog or a previous unpacked load. The exact scenario gh-1616 enables — iterate on a widget with Fa, then load a worktree folder with the same id — silently replaces the agent-built code with only a generic confirm.

Fix: treat "an app with this id already exists" as the replace condition, and label the unknown source honestly, e.g.:

```dart
final replaces = existingApp != null;
...
existingSource: existingApp == null
    ? null
    : (existingApp.installSource ?? /* agent-created label */),
```

(the `unpackedLoadReplaceNote` copy needs a third source variant, e.g. "created by the agent"). A test where the existing app has no install record would pin it.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the unpacked badge and the seed-error badge occupy the same corner — one hides the other**

Both badges are `Positioned(top: -3, right: -3)` and stack on the same tile corner:

```dart
child: _maybeUnpackedBadge(
  colors,
  key,
  _maybeSeedErrorBadge(colors, key, _tileIcon(colors, key)),
),
```

`_maybeUnpackedBadge` wraps the seed-error Stack and paints its 14×14 indigo folder badge **after** (on top of) the 16×16 error badge. When both apply — an unpacked-loaded widget whose manifest the agent later edits into garbage (`_appsById[id]?.error != null`) — the doc comment's promise "both can show at once" holds only in the widget tree: visually the folder badge covers the error badge, so the "manifest is broken, tap for the copyable error" affordance disappears exactly when the unpacked widget breaks.

Fix: move the unpacked badge to the opposite corner (e.g. `top: -3, left: -3`), or compose the two indicators side by side in one Stack. Note the error badge is reachable for unpacked apps (it is not demo-only: the `error` branch fires for any unparseable manifest), so this is a real failure-path UI bug, though not data loss.

💡 **SUGGESTION: unused import — `package:flutter/material.dart`**

```text
warning - unpacked_load_golden_test.dart:13:8 - Unused import:
'package:flutter/material.dart'. ... unused_import
```

The new golden test uses only `flutter_test`, the flow widgets and `Uint8List`. This is the only analyzer finding in the whole PR (everything else in `flutter analyze` for the touched files is pre-existing) — drop line 13 to keep the new file warning-clean.

💡 **SUGGESTION: hardcode `'Load unpacked'` duplicates the new `launcherLoadUnpacked` l10n key**

This PR adds the arb key `launcherLoadUnpacked` ("Load unpacked" / ru "Загрузить папку") and uses it in the launcher tab row — but this second entry point hardcodes the English string:

```dart
label: const Text('Load unpacked'),
```

The file carries a grandfathered `// l10n:ignore-file` opt-out (hence `'Get widgets'` above is also literal), so the guard stays green — but the key is right there and ru-locale users get English here while the launcher row next to the same feature is translated. One-line fix: `label: Text(context.l10n.launcherLoadUnpacked)`.

While that runs, let me do the exhaustive re-read pass on the changed files for anything missed. Let me re-check a few things:

1. `unpacked_load_flow.dart` — the `existing` lookup: `existing.where((app) => app.id == inspection.id).toList()` — `listApps()` returns apps keyed by DIRECTORY name as id (`JsAppInfo.fromManifest(decoded, bundled: false, fallbackId: id)` — id = manifest id or fallback dir name). Note: an app's `id` comes from the MANIFEST, not the dir name. The install writes to `apps/<manifest-id>/`. If a DIFFERENT directory contains a manifest declaring the same id (agent-created app in `apps/foo/` declaring `id: fa-agents`), the replace check finds it (id match), confirm shown — good. Install overwrites `apps/fa-agents/` — the OTHER folder `apps/foo/` still exists with a duplicate id! Edge case: two dirs, same manifest id. The grid would show two tiles with the same id. That's a pre-existing general quirk (agent-created apps), not introduced here. Skip.

2. `UnpackedLoadConfirmDialog` — `existingSource` null → `replaces` false — but what about an existing AGENT-CREATED app (no install record, installSource null)? `existingApp != null` but `existingSource == null` → `replaces = false` → NO replace warning shown, confirm button says "Load", yet the load OVERWRITES an existing agent-created widget's files (storage.json kept, code overwritten). The ticket AC4: "replacing an existing id asks for confirmation". The confirmation IS still shown (the whole load is confirmed), but the explicit REPLACE WARNING is skipped for agent-created apps — the user isn't told they're overwriting existing work. Hmm wait — actually re-read:

```dart
final replaced = existing.where((app) => app.id == inspection.id).toList();
final existingApp = replaced.isEmpty ? null : replaced.first;
```

Then `existingSource: existingApp?.installSource` — for an agent-created app, installSource is null → `replaces = existingSource != null` → false. So overwriting an agent-created app shows NO replace warning. The dialog in that case looks identical to a fresh load. The version line `existingVersion: existingApp?.version` also dropped.

Is that a real gap? The ticket AC4 says "replacing an existing id asks for confirmation" — the load itself always asks for confirmation (the capability confirm), so technically an ask happens. But the REPLACE semantics (naming the old install) only trigger when there's an install record. For agent-created apps (no record) the user gets no overwrite warning. That's a genuine finding — IMPORTANT (the dialog misleads: overwriting existing work without the warning banner). Fix: `replaces` should key off `existingApp != null`, with source falling back to something like "created by the agent".

Let me verify the current dialog logic once more... Yes:

```dart
final replaces = existingSource != null;
```

And the flow passes `existingSource: existingApp?.installSource` (null for agent-created). So the replace note only renders when the old install has a recorded origin. Agent-created apps → silent overwrite. IMPORTANT.

3. `loadUnpackedWidget` — `if (picked.isEmpty || !context.mounted) return;` — an empty pick returns silently. Good (E1).

4. Web picker — `readFileFully` reads files SEQUENTIALLY in a for loop — fine for ≤10MiB caps.

5. The `FolderPicker` interface lives in `unpacked_loader.dart` (lib/apps) while implementations live in lib/services — the services file imports from apps. Layering: services → apps import. Other services import apps? e.g. flutter_app/lib/services/... let me check if services importing apps is an established direction. The seed badge pattern is nearly identical (Stack + Positioned + Container + icon) — consistent. But notice: **both badges occupy the SAME corner (top: -3, right: -3)**. `_maybeUnpackedBadge` wraps the tile and `_maybeSeedErrorBadge` wraps the icon — the composition order is `_maybeUnpackedBadge(colors, key, _maybeSeedErrorBadge(...))` — the unpacked badge Stack CONTAINS the seed-error Stack. Both Positioned at top:-3/right:-3 → **they overlap exactly**; when both show (unpacked + seed error), the 14px indigo folder badge sits ON TOP of the 16px seed-error badge (later in Stack paint order → unpacked badge covers the error badge). The doc comment claims "Composes with the seed-error badge (both can show at once)" — but visually they'd stack on the same corner and hide the error indicator!

Wait — actually, can an unpacked app have failedSeeds? `failedSeeds` is for demo seed failures — demoAppIds is EMPTY, so failedSeeds never populates anymore ("nothing is seeded"). But the OTHER condition: `_appsById[id]?.error != null` — an app whose manifest no longer parses (agent edit). An unpacked app whose manifest gets corrupted (or agent edits it into garbage) → error badge condition true → both badges → overlap → error badge hidden behind the unpacked badge (painted after? The unpacked badge Stack's child is the seed-badge Stack; within the outer Stack, children paint in order: tile (containing seed badge), then the unpacked badge Positioned — the unpacked badge paints LAST = on top).

So yes: an unpacked app with a broken manifest shows only the folder badge; the error badge is fully covered (14px over 16px, offset same). The comment says "both can show at once" — they CAN, but one hides the other. This is a real UI bug — the error indicator (the "hand the error to Fa" affordance) disappears exactly when an unpacked widget breaks. Severity: IMPORTANT (misleading UI in the failure path; not data loss/crash). Fix: offset the unpacked badge to the opposite corner (top-left) or compose them side by side.

Let me double-check paint order and geometry: seed badge: top:-3 right:-3, 16x16. Unpacked: top:-3 right:-3, 14x14 with 2px bg-colored border. The unpacked badge (outer Stack, later child) paints over. The 16px error badge would show a 1px ring at edges — mostly hidden. Effectively hidden. Confirmed.

Wait — actually let me re-read the composition:

```dart
child: _maybeUnpackedBadge(
  colors,
  key,
  _maybeSeedErrorBadge(colors, key, _tileIcon(colors, key)),
```

_maybeSeedErrorBadge returns a Stack [tile, Positioned(error badge)] when failed. _maybeUnpackedBadge wraps THAT in Stack [that, Positioned(unpacked badge)]. Both Positioned identical corner. Outer Stack's unpacked badge is the last child → paints on top. Confirmed overlap.

Hmm — although… is it truly "hidden"? The unpacked badge is 14x14 with a 2px border colored `colors.bg` (tile background) — so visually it's a circle with the folder icon; the error badge's 16x16 would peek out 1px around. Effectively the error state is unreadable. Yes, IMPORTANT.

Next, check `_appsById` — does it exist? It's used by both badges (seed badge uses `_appsById[id]?.error`). Fine.

Now let me also reconsider the CI failure severity decision. Facts:
- The PR's CI run (dispatch on 205a6fc0) failed on TWO jobs, both traced to `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 0/3)` failing `skills_freshness_pty_test.dart` (a root-package CLI test; PR touches only flutter_app/**).
- main's tip (66c30d923, the direct merge parent) passed the same shard with the same test.
- The repo documents PTY flakiness + a quarantine process (gh-1199 AC6, #1469), and there's an entire branch named after flaky PTY timing flakes.

Per the machine protocol: "🚨 BLOCKING — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates (red CI)...". The CI is red → BLOCKING → REQUEST_CHANGES. F7 also says include each ci_failures.md failure as 🚨 BLOCKING. I'll follow that: recommendation REQUEST_CHANGES, blocking count 1 (the red CI leg, explicitly noted as unrelated-to-diff flake-suspect but red gate = merge blocked; REG-1 in the ticket: red CI blocks merge).

Hmm, but wait — think about this carefully. The verdict rules say REQUEST_CHANGES with blocking ≥ 1 triggers a REWORK round (15-20 CI min). A rework round would just re-dispatch CI and likely go green (flake). The alternative: APPROVE with the CI failure noted... but the machine would then merge a PR whose required gate is RED? No — branch protection handles that independently: the Quality gate is a required check; the machine merges only when green (per AGENTS.md gh-1537: "dispatches ci.yml on the updated head, and merges only when green"). {"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a whitespace-padded manifest id is validated trimmed but installed untrimmed**

`WidgetPayloadValidation.id` returns the **raw** `manifest['id']` (untrimmed), while `_checkSchema` validates the **trimmed** form (`rawId.trim()` → `_checkId`) and `WidgetManifest.fromJson` also trims. So a manifest like:

```json
{"id": " fa-agents ", "name": "X", "version": "1.0.0"}
```

passes validation (the id rule `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` is enforced on the trimmed value), and then this line installs it into a **space-padded folder**:

```dart
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: id, // " fa-agents " — written as apps/ fa-agents /manifest.json
  ...
```

Verified locally: `inspection.id` = `" fa-agents "` and the env ends up with `apps/ fa-agents /` + a `.installed.json` key `" fa-agents "` — the stored id violates the very rule the validator just enforced. No traversal risk (regex rejects `/` and `..`), but the widget's stored id no longer matches the id rule, and the folder name carries whitespace everywhere (grid key, `open_app`, records).

Fix (one line, in `UnpackedWidgetLoader.install`):

```dart
final trimmed = id.trim();
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: trimmed,
  version: inspection.version ?? '0.0.0',
  files: inspection.files,
  origin: origin,
);
```

—or reject ids where `id != id.trim()` in the validator with a named `id_invalid` error. A regression test with a padded id belongs in `unpacked_loader_test.dart`.
"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the replace warning is skipped for agent-created apps — their code is overwritten silently**

The replace check keys off the install record:

```dart
final replaced = existing.where((app) => app.id == inspection.id).toList();
final existingApp = replaced.isEmpty ? null : replaced.first;
...
existingSource: existingApp?.installSource, // null for agent-created apps
```

and the dialog decides `final replaces = existingSource != null;`.

An **agent-created** app (built with Fa via file tools) has **no** `.installed.json` record, so `installSource` is `null` → `replaces` is `false` → the dialog renders as a plain fresh-load confirm ("Load" button, no warning banner), even though confirming **overwrites that app's code** (`installWidget` only protects files whose hashes are recorded — an agent-created app has none, so every file is replaced; only `storage.json` survives).

Ticket AC4 says "replacing an existing id asks for confirmation" — the load confirm still appears, but the explicit replace warning (naming what is being replaced) fires only when the old install came from the catalog or a previous unpacked load. The exact scenario gh-1616 enables — iterate on a widget with Fa, then load a worktree folder with the same id — silently replaces the agent-built code with only a generic confirm.

Fix: treat "an app with this id already exists" as the replace condition, and label the unknown source honestly, e.g.:

```dart
final replaces = existingApp != null;
...
existingSource: existingApp == null
    ? null
    : (existingApp.installSource ?? /* agent-created label */),
```

(the `unpackedLoadReplaceNote` copy needs a third source variant, e.g. "created by the agent"). A test where the existing app has no install record would pin it.

While that runs, let me do the exhaustive re-read pass on the changed files for anything missed. Let me re-check a few things:

1. `unpacked_load_flow.dart` — the `existing` lookup: `existing.where((app) => app.id == inspection.id).toList()` — `listApps()` returns apps keyed by DIRECTORY name as id (`JsAppInfo.fromManifest(decoded, bundled: false, fallbackId: id)` — id = manifest id or fallback dir name). Note: an app's `id` comes from the MANIFEST, not the dir name. The install writes to `apps/<manifest-id>/`. If a DIFFERENT directory contains a manifest declaring the same id (agent-created app in `apps/foo/` declaring `id: fa-agents`), the replace check finds it (id match), confirm shown — good. Install overwrites `apps/fa-agents/` — the OTHER folder `apps/foo/` still exists with a duplicate id! Edge case: two dirs, same manifest id. The grid would show two tiles with the same id. That's a pre-existing general quirk (agent-created apps), not introduced here. Skip.

2. `UnpackedLoadConfirmDialog` — `existingSource` null → `replaces` false — but what about an existing AGENT-CREATED app (no install record, installSource null)? `existingApp != null` but `existingSource == null` → `replaces = false` → NO replace warning shown, confirm button says "Load", yet the load OVERWRITES an existing agent-created widget's files (storage.json kept, code overwritten). The ticket AC4: "replacing an existing id asks for confirmation". The confirmation IS still shown (the whole load is confirmed), but the explicit REPLACE WARNING is skipped for agent-created apps — the user isn't told they're overwriting existing work. Hmm wait — actually re-read:

```dart
final replaced = existing.where((app) => app.id == inspection.id).toList();
final existingApp = replaced.isEmpty ? null : replaced.first;
```

Then `existingSource: existingApp?.installSource` — for an agent-created app, installSource is null → `replaces = existingSource != null` → false. So overwriting an agent-created app shows NO replace warning. The dialog in that case looks identical to a fresh load. The version line `existingVersion: existingApp?.version` also dropped.

Is that a real gap? The ticket AC4 says "replacing an existing id asks for confirmation" — the load itself always asks for confirmation (the capability confirm), so technically an ask happens. But the REPLACE semantics (naming the old install) only trigger when there's an install record. For agent-created apps (no record) the user gets no overwrite warning. That's a genuine finding — IMPORTANT (the dialog misleads: overwriting existing work without the warning banner). Fix: `replaces` should key off `existingApp != null`, with source falling back to something like "created by the agent".

Let me verify the current dialog logic once more... Yes:

```dart
final replaces = existingSource != null;
```

And the flow passes `existingSource: existingApp?.installSource` (null for agent-created). So the replace note only renders when the old install has a recorded origin. Agent-created apps → silent overwrite. IMPORTANT.

3. `loadUnpackedWidget` — `if (picked.isEmpty || !context.mounted) return;` — an empty pick returns silently. Good (E1).

4. Web picker — `readFileFully` reads files SEQUENTIALLY in a for loop — fine for ≤10MiB caps.

Both Positioned at top:-3/right:-3 → **they overlap exactly**; when both show (unpacked + seed error), the 14px indigo folder badge sits ON TOP of the 16px seed-error badge (later in Stack paint order → unpacked badge covers the error badge). The doc comment claims "Composes with the seed-error badge (both can show at once)" — but visually they'd stack on the same corner and hide the error indicator!

Wait — actually, can an unpacked app have failedSeeds? `failedSeeds` is for demo seed failures — demoAppIds is EMPTY, so failedSeeds never populates anymore ("nothing is seeded"). But the OTHER condition: `_appsById[id]?.error != null` — an app whose manifest no longer parses (agent edit). An unpacked app whose manifest gets corrupted (or agent edits it into garbage) → error badge condition true → both badges → overlap → error badge hidden behind the unpacked badge (painted after? The unpacked badge Stack's child is the seed-badge Stack; within the outer Stack, children paint in order: tile (containing seed badge), then the unpacked badge Positioned — the unpacked badge paints LAST = on top).

So yes: an unpacked app with a broken manifest shows only the folder badge; the error badge is fully covered (14px over 16px, offset same). The comment says "both can show at once" — they CAN, but one hides the other. This is a real UI bug — the error indicator (the "hand the error to Fa" affordance) disappears exactly when an unpacked widget breaks. Severity: IMPORTANT (misleading UI in the failure path; not data loss/crash). Fix: offset the unpacked badge to the opposite corner (top-left) or compose them side by side.

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a whitespace-padded manifest id is validated trimmed but installed untrimmed**

`WidgetPayloadValidation.id` returns the **raw** `manifest['id']` (untrimmed), while `_checkSchema` validates the **trimmed** form (`rawId.trim()` → `_checkId`) and `WidgetManifest.fromJson` also trims. So a manifest like:

```json
{"id": " fa-agents ", "name": "X", "version": "1.0.0"}
```

passes validation (the id rule `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` is enforced on the trimmed value), and then this line installs it into a **space-padded folder**:

```dart
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: id, // " fa-agents " — written as apps/ fa-agents /manifest.json
  ...
```

Verified locally: `inspection.id` = `" fa-agents "` and the env ends up with `apps/ fa-agents /` + a `.installed.json` key `" fa-agents "` — the stored id violates the very rule the validator just enforced. No traversal risk (regex rejects `/` and `..`), but the widget's stored id no longer matches the id rule, and the folder name carries whitespace everywhere (grid key, `open_app`, records).

Fix (one line, in `UnpackedWidgetLoader.install`):

```dart
final trimmed = id.trim();
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: trimmed,
  version: inspection.version ?? '0.0.0',
  files: inspection.files,
  origin: origin,
);
```

—or reject ids where `id != id.trim()` in the validator with a named `id_invalid` error. A regression test with a padded id belongs in `unpacked_loader_test.dart`.
"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the replace warning is skipped for agent-created apps — their code is overwritten silently**

The replace check keys off the install record:

```dart
final replaced = existing.where((app) => app.id == inspection.id).toList();
final existingApp = replaced.isEmpty ? null : replaced.first;
...
existingSource: existingApp?.installSource, // null for agent-created apps
```

and the dialog decides `final replaces = existingSource != null;`.

An **agent-created** app (built with Fa via file tools) has **no** `.installed.json` record, so `installSource` is `null` → `replaces` is `false` → the dialog renders as a plain fresh-load confirm ("Load" button, no warning banner), even though confirming **overwrites that app's code** (`installWidget` only protects files whose hashes are recorded — an agent-created app has none, so every file is replaced; only `storage.json` survives).

Ticket AC4 says "replacing an existing id asks for confirmation" — the load confirm still appears, but the explicit replace warning (naming what is being replaced) fires only when the old install came from the catalog or a previous unpacked load. The exact scenario gh-1616 enables — iterate on a widget with Fa, then load a worktree folder with the same id — silently replaces the agent-built code with only a generic confirm.

Fix: treat "an app with this id already exists" as the replace condition, and label the unknown source honestly, e.g.:

```dart
final replaces = existingApp != null;
...
existingSource: existingApp == null
    ? null
    : (existingApp.installSource ?? /* agent-created label */),
```

(the `unpackedLoadReplaceNote` copy needs a third source variant, e.g. "created by the agent"). A test where the existing app has no install record would pin it.

Good — but hold on: in `listApps`, `_withI18nContents` runs BEFORE `withInstallSource` is applied (sources attached after cache gate). The cached app (`_parsedApps[id]`) — is cached WITH installSource from a previous scan? `withInstallSource` returns `this` when `installSource == source` — and `_parsedApps` stores the app as last parsed... Let me trace: first scan: app parsed (installSource=null) → withInstallSource('catalog') creates a copy → `_parsedApps[id]` was set BEFORE the copy (line `_parsedApps[id] = app;` then at the end `withInstallSource`). So the cache holds the null-source version; each scan re-derives source from the record. That's exactly the documented design ("the badge must follow the record, not the cached parse"). Good — no stale-source bug.

6. **`listApps` error path** (`entries == null`): attaches sources to cached apps — consistent.

7. **Danger check — `installSources()` double-read**: in listApps normal path, `_readInstalled` may be called up to 3 times (prune + installSources). Web OPFS reads are cheap-ish; the whole listApps already reads each manifest. Acceptable. Not flagging.

8. **`_checkId` dedup logic** — `errors.any((error) => error.code == 'id_invalid' && error.message.contains("'$id'"))` — raw id check then parsed id check. If raw id = 'FOO' and parsed id = '' (empty after stringField error)... wait, if 'id' must be a non-empty string error is present, `rawId` is null/empty → skipped; parsed.id = '' → `_checkId('')` → idPattern fails → error "manifest id '' must match..." — hmm, that's a confusing double error: "'id' must be a non-empty string" AND "manifest id '' must match [a-z0-9]...". Minor noise. Let me verify: manifest `{"name": "X", "version": "1.0.0"}` (no id). `rawId = stamped['id']` → null → skip raw check. `WidgetManifest.fromJson(stamped)` → errors "'id' must be a non-empty string" → ManifestException → caught → only that error. OK good — no parsed.id when the parser throws. Fine.

What if id = '  ' (whitespace)? rawId.trim().isEmpty → skip raw. Parser: stringField trims, empty → error. Fine.

What if id is a number, e.g. `"id": 123`? rawId is String check fails → skip. Parser: `123 is! String` → error "'id' must be a non-empty string". Fine.

What if id = 'valid-id' but ALSO name missing? Parser throws on name; id error from raw check already added. Both errors surface in one pass — that's the documented "one round" goal. Good.

9. **`WidgetPayloadValidation.id` getter** returns `manifest?['id']?.toString()` — the RAW id, not trimmed. If manifest id = ' fa-agents ' (with spaces): raw check `rawId.trim()` → 'fa-agents' valid → no error. {"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a whitespace-padded manifest id is validated trimmed but installed untrimmed**

`WidgetPayloadValidation.id` returns the **raw** `manifest['id']` (untrimmed), while `_checkSchema` validates the **trimmed** form (`rawId.trim()` → `_checkId`) and `WidgetManifest.fromJson` also trims. So a manifest like:

```json
{"id": " fa-agents ", "name": "X", "version": "1.0.0"}
```

passes validation (the id rule `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` is enforced on the trimmed value), and then this line installs it into a **space-padded folder**:

```dart
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: id, // " fa-agents " — written as apps/ fa-agents /manifest.json
  ...
```

Verified locally: `inspection.id` = `" fa-agents "` and the env ends up with `apps/ fa-agents /` + a `.installed.json` key `" fa-agents "` — the stored id violates the very rule the validator just enforced. No traversal risk (regex rejects `/` and `..`), but the widget's stored id no longer matches the id rule, and the folder name carries whitespace everywhere (grid key, `open_app`, records).

Fix (one line, in `UnpackedWidgetLoader.install`):

```dart
final trimmed = id.trim();
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: trimmed,
  version: inspection.version ?? '0.0.0',
  files: inspection.files,
  origin: origin,
);
```

—or reject ids where `id != id.trim()` in the validator with a named `id_invalid` error. A regression test with a padded id belongs in `unpacked_loader_test.dart`.
"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the replace warning is skipped for agent-created apps — their code is overwritten silently**

The replace check keys off the install record:

```dart
final replaced = existing.where((app) => app.id == inspection.id).toList();
final existingApp = replaced.isEmpty ? null : replaced.first;
...
existingSource: existingApp?.installSource, // null for agent-created apps
```

and the dialog decides `final replaces = existingSource != null;`.

An **agent-created** app (built with Fa via file tools) has **no** `.installed.json` record, so `installSource` is `null` → `replaces` is `false` → the dialog renders as a plain fresh-load confirm ("Load" button, no warning banner), even though confirming **overwrites that app's code** (`installWidget` only protects files whose hashes are recorded — an agent-created app has none, so every file is replaced; only `storage.json` survives).

Ticket AC4 says "replacing an existing id asks for confirmation" — the load confirm still appears, but the explicit replace warning (naming what is being replaced) fires only when the old install came from the catalog or a previous unpacked load. The exact scenario gh-1616 enables — iterate on a widget with Fa, then load a worktree folder with the same id — silently replaces the agent-built code with only a generic confirm.

Fix: treat "an app with this id already exists" as the replace condition, and label the unknown source honestly, e.g.:

```dart
final replaces = existingApp != null;
...
existingSource: existingApp == null
    ? null
    : (existingApp.installSource ?? /* agent-created label */),
```

(the `unpackedLoadReplaceNote` copy needs a third source variant, e.g. "created by the agent"). A test where the existing app has no install record would pin it.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the unpacked badge and the seed-error badge occupy the same corner — one hides the other**

Both badges are `Positioned(top: -3, right: -3)` and stack on the same tile corner:

```dart
child: _maybeUnpackedBadge(
  colors,
  key,
  _maybeSeedErrorBadge(colors, key, _tileIcon(colors, key)),
),
```

`_maybeUnpackedBadge` wraps the seed-error Stack and paints its 14×14 indigo folder badge **after** (on top of) the 16×16 error badge. When both apply — an unpacked-loaded widget whose manifest the agent later edits into garbage (`_appsById[id]?.error != null`) — the doc comment's promise "both can show at once" holds only in the widget tree: visually the folder badge covers the error badge, so the "manifest is broken, tap for the copyable error" affordance disappears exactly when the unpacked widget breaks.

Fix: move the unpacked badge to the opposite corner (e.g. `top: -3, left: -3`), or compose the two indicators side by side in one Stack. Note the error badge is reachable for unpacked apps (it is not demo-only: the `error` branch fires for any unparseable manifest), so this is a real failure-path UI bug, though not data loss.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: hardcode `'Load unpacked'` duplicates the new `launcherLoadUnpacked` l10n key**

This PR adds the arb key `launcherLoadUnpacked` ("Load unpacked" / ru "Загрузить папку") and uses it in the launcher tab row — but this second entry point hardcodes the English string:

```dart
label: const Text('Load unpacked'),
```

The file carries a grandfathered `// l10n:ignore-file` opt-out (hence `'Get widgets'` above is also literal), so the guard stays green — but the key is right there and ru-locale users get English here while the launcher row next to the same feature is translated. One-line fix: `label: Text(context.l10n.launcherLoadUnpacked)`.

The cached app (`_parsedApps[id]`) — is cached WITH installSource from a previous scan? `withInstallSource` returns `this` when `installSource == source` — and `_parsedApps` stores the app as last parsed... Let me trace: first scan: app parsed (installSource=null) → withInstallSource('catalog') creates a copy → `_parsedApps[id]` was set BEFORE the copy (line `_parsedApps[id] = app;` then at the end `withInstallSource`). While that runs, let me do the exhaustive re-read pass on the changed files for anything missed. Let me re-check a few things:

1. `unpacked_load_flow.dart` — the `existing` lookup: `existing.where((app) => app.id == inspection.id).toList()` — `listApps()` returns apps keyed by DIRECTORY name as id (`JsAppInfo.fromManifest(decoded, bundled: false, fallbackId: id)` — id = manifest id or fallback dir name). Note: an app's `id` comes from the MANIFEST, not the dir name. The install writes to `apps/<manifest-id>/`. If a DIFFERENT directory contains a manifest declaring the same id (agent-created app in `apps/foo/` declaring `id: fa-agents`), the replace check finds it (id match), confirm shown — good. Install overwrites `apps/fa-agents/` — the OTHER folder `apps/foo/` still exists with a duplicate id! Edge case: two dirs, same manifest id. The grid would show two tiles with the same id. That's a pre-existing general quirk (agent-created apps), not introduced here. Skip.

2. `UnpackedLoadConfirmDialog` — `existingSource` null → `replaces` false — but what about an existing AGENT-CREATED app (no install record, installSource null)? `existingApp != null` but `existingSource == null` → `replaces = false` → NO replace warning shown, confirm button says "Load", yet the load OVERWRITES an existing agent-created widget's files (storage.json kept, code overwritten). The ticket AC4: "replacing an existing id asks for confirmation". The confirmation IS still shown (the whole load is confirmed), but the explicit REPLACE WARNING is skipped for agent-created apps — the user isn't told they're overwriting existing work. Hmm wait — actually re-read:

```dart
final replaced = existing.where((app) => app.id == inspection.id).toList();
final existingApp = replaced.isEmpty ? null : replaced.first;
```

Then `existingSource: existingApp?.installSource` — for an agent-created app, installSource is null → `replaces = existingSource != null` → false. So overwriting an agent-created app shows NO replace warning. The dialog in that case looks identical to a fresh load. The version line `existingVersion: existingApp?.version` also dropped.

Is that a real gap? The ticket AC4 says "replacing an existing id asks for confirmation" — the load itself always asks for confirmation (the capability confirm), so technically an ask happens. But the REPLACE semantics (naming the old install) only trigger when there's an install record. For agent-created apps (no record) the user gets no overwrite warning. That's a genuine finding — IMPORTANT (the dialog misleads: overwriting existing work without the warning banner). Fix: `replaces` should key off `existingApp != null`, with source falling back to something like "created by the agent".


And the flow passes `existingSource: existingApp?.installSource` (null for agent-created). So the replace note only renders when the old install has a recorded origin. Agent-created apps → silent overwrite. IMPORTANT.

3. `loadUnpackedWidget` — `if (picked.isEmpty || !context.mounted) return;` — an empty pick returns silently. Good (E1).

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a whitespace-padded manifest id is validated trimmed but installed untrimmed**

`WidgetPayloadValidation.id` returns the **raw** `manifest['id']` (untrimmed), while `_checkSchema` validates the **trimmed** form (`rawId.trim()` → `_checkId`) and `WidgetManifest.fromJson` also trims. So a manifest like:

```json
{"id": " fa-agents ", "name": "X", "version": "1.0.0"}
```

passes validation (the id rule `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` is enforced on the trimmed value), and then this line installs it into a **space-padded folder**:

```dart
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: id, // " fa-agents " — written as apps/ fa-agents /manifest.json
  ...
```

Verified locally: `inspection.id` = `" fa-agents "` and the env ends up with `apps/ fa-agents /` + a `.installed.json` key `" fa-agents "` — the stored id violates the very rule the validator just enforced. No traversal risk (regex rejects `/` and `..`), but the widget's stored id no longer matches the id rule, and the folder name carries whitespace everywhere (grid key, `open_app`, records).

Fix (one line, in `UnpackedWidgetLoader.install`):

```dart
final trimmed = id.trim();
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: trimmed,
  version: inspection.version ?? '0.0.0',
  files: inspection.files,
  origin: origin,
);
```

—or reject ids where `id != id.trim()` in the validator with a named `id_invalid` error. A regression test with a padded id belongs in `unpacked_loader_test.dart`.
"}

The replace check keys off the install record:

```dart
final replaced = existing.where((app) => app.id == inspection.id).toList();
final existingApp = replaced.isEmpty ? null : replaced.first;
...
existingSource: existingApp?.installSource, // null for agent-created apps
```

and the dialog decides `final replaces = existingSource != null;`.

An **agent-created** app (built with Fa via file tools) has **no** `.installed.json` record, so `installSource` is `null` → `replaces` is `false` → the dialog renders as a plain fresh-load confirm ("Load" button, no warning banner), even though confirming **overwrites that app's code** (`installWidget` only protects files whose hashes are recorded — an agent-created app has none, so every file is replaced; only `storage.json` survives).

The exact scenario gh-1616 enables — iterate on a widget with Fa, then load a worktree folder with the same id — silently replaces the agent-built code with only a generic confirm.

Fix: treat "an app with this id already exists" as the replace condition, and label the unknown source honestly, e.g.:

```dart
final replaces = existingApp != null;
...
existingSource: existingApp == null
    ? null
    : (existingApp.installSource ?? /* agent-created label */),
```

(the `unpackedLoadReplaceNote` copy needs a third source variant, e.g. "created by the agent"). A test where the existing app has no install record would pin it.

5. **`withI18nContents`** now carries `installSource` through — wait, in the diff, `withI18nContents` got `installSource: installSource` added. Good — but hold on: in `listApps`, `_withI18nContents` runs BEFORE `withInstallSource` is applied (sources attached after cache gate). The cached app (`_parsedApps[id]`) — is cached WITH installSource from a previous scan? `withInstallSource` returns `this` when `installSource == source` — and `_parsedApps` stores the app as last parsed... Let me trace: first scan: app parsed (installSource=null) → withInstallSource('catalog') creates a copy → `_parsedApps[id]` was set BEFORE the copy (line `_parsedApps[id] = app;` then at the end `withInstallSource`). So the cache holds the null-source version; each scan re-derives source from the record. That's exactly the documented design ("the badge must follow the record, not the cached parse"). Good — no stale-source bug.

6. **`listApps` error path** (`entries == null`): attaches sources to cached apps — consistent.

If raw id = 'FOO' and parsed id = '' (empty after stringField error)... wait, if 'id' must be a non-empty string error is present, `rawId` is null/empty → skipped; parsed.id = '' → `_checkId('')` → idPattern fails → error "manifest id '' must match..." — hmm, that's a confusing double error: "'id' must be a non-empty string" AND "manifest id '' must match [a-z0-9]...". OK good — no parsed.id when the parser throws. Fine.

What if id = '  ' (whitespace)? rawId.trim().isEmpty → skip raw. Parser: stringField trims, empty → error. Fine.

What if id is a number, e.g. `"id": 123`? rawId is String check fails → skip. Parser: `123 is! String` → error "'id' must be a non-empty string". Fine.

What if id = 'valid-id' but ALSO name missing? Parser throws on name; id error from raw check already added. Both errors surface in one pass — that's the documented "one round" goal. Good.

If manifest id = ' fa-agents ' (with spaces): raw check `rawId.trim()` → 'fa-agents' valid → no error. Parsed.id — parser trims → 'fa-agents'. isValid → true. install uses `inspection.id` = raw ' fa-agents ' → `installWidget(id: ' fa-agents ')` → writes `apps/ fa-agents /manifest.json` — a folder with spaces in the name! The app's manifest id parsed by JsAppInfo.fromManifest = ' fa-agents '.toString() — with spaces.

So a manifest with `"id": " fa-agents "` (leading/trailing spaces) PASSES validation (both raw-trimmed and parsed checks pass) but installs into `apps/ fa-agents /` with a space-padded folder name. That's a real (if narrow) correctness bug: the installed id diverges from the validated id; the badge/records would still line up (all use the same padded string), but the widget is stored under a name that violates the id rule the validator just enforced; boot probably still works (folder name is just a directory). Note: an app's `id` comes from the MANIFEST, not the dir name. The install writes to `apps/<manifest-id>/`. If a DIFFERENT directory contains a manifest declaring the same id (agent-created app in `apps/foo/` declaring `id: fa-agents`), the replace check finds it (id match), confirm shown — good. Install overwrites `apps/fa-agents/` — the OTHER folder `apps/foo/` still exists with a duplicate id! Edge case: two dirs, same manifest id. The grid would show two tiles with the same id. That's a pre-existing general quirk (agent-created apps), not introduced here. Skip.

2. `UnpackedLoadConfirmDialog` — `existingSource` null → `replaces` false — but what about an existing AGENT-CREATED app (no install record, installSource null)? `existingApp != null` but `existingSource == null` → `replaces = false` → NO replace warning shown, confirm button says "Load", yet the load OVERWRITES an existing agent-created widget's files (storage.json kept, code overwritten). The ticket AC4: "replacing an existing id asks for confirmation". The confirmation IS still shown (the whole load is confirmed), but the explicit REPLACE WARNING is skipped for agent-created apps — the user isn't told they're overwriting existing work.
```dart
final replaced = existing.where((app) => app.id == inspection.id).toList();
final existingApp = replaced.isEmpty ? null : replaced.first;
```

Then `existingSource: existingApp?.installSource` — for an agent-created app, installSource is null → `replaces = existingSource != null` → false. So overwriting an agent-created app shows NO replace warning. The dialog in that case looks identical to a fresh load. The version line `existingVersion: existingApp?.version` also dropped.

Is that a real gap? The ticket AC4 says "replacing an existing id asks for confirmation" — the load itself always asks for confirmation (the capability confirm), so technically an ask happens. But the REPLACE semantics (naming the old install) only trigger when there's an install record. For agent-created apps (no record) the user gets no overwrite warning. That's a genuine finding — IMPORTANT (the dialog misleads: overwriting existing work without the warning banner). {"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a whitespace-padded manifest id is validated trimmed but installed untrimmed**

`WidgetPayloadValidation.id` returns the **raw** `manifest['id']` (untrimmed), while `_checkSchema` validates the **trimmed** form (`rawId.trim()` → `_checkId`) and `WidgetManifest.fromJson` also trims. So a manifest like:

```json
{"id": " fa-agents ", "name": "X", "version": "1.0.0"}
```

passes validation (the id rule `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` is enforced on the trimmed value), and then this line installs it into a **space-padded folder**:

```dart
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: id, // " fa-agents " — written as apps/ fa-agents /manifest.json
  ...
```

Verified locally: `inspection.id` = `" fa-agents "` and the env ends up with `apps/ fa-agents /` + a `.installed.json` key `" fa-agents "` — the stored id violates the very rule the validator just enforced. No traversal risk (regex rejects `/` and `..`), but the widget's stored id no longer matches the id rule, and the folder name carries whitespace everywhere (grid key, `open_app`, records).

Fix (one line, in `UnpackedWidgetLoader.install`):

```dart
final trimmed = id.trim();
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: trimmed,
  version: inspection.version ?? '0.0.0',
  files: inspection.files,
  origin: origin,
);
```

—or reject ids where `id != id.trim()` in the validator with a named `id_invalid` error. A regression test with a padded id belongs in `unpacked_loader_test.dart`.
"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the replace warning is skipped for agent-created apps — their code is overwritten silently**

The replace check keys off the install record:

```dart
final replaced = existing.where((app) => app.id == inspection.id).toList();
final existingApp = replaced.isEmpty ? null : replaced.first;
...
existingSource: existingApp?.installSource, // null for agent-created apps
```

and the dialog decides `final replaces = existingSource != null;`.

An **agent-created** app (built with Fa via file tools) has **no** `.installed.json` record, so `installSource` is `null` → `replaces` is `false` → the dialog renders as a plain fresh-load confirm ("Load" button, no warning banner), even though confirming **overwrites that app's code** (`installWidget` only protects files whose hashes are recorded — an agent-created app has none, so every file is replaced; only `storage.json` survives).

Ticket AC4 says "replacing an existing id asks for confirmation" — the load confirm still appears, but the explicit replace warning (naming what is being replaced) fires only when the old install came from the catalog or a previous unpacked load. The exact scenario gh-1616 enables — iterate on a widget with Fa, then load a worktree folder with the same id — silently replaces the agent-built code with only a generic confirm.

Fix: treat "an app with this id already exists" as the replace condition, and label the unknown source honestly, e.g.:

```dart
final replaces = existingApp != null;
...
existingSource: existingApp == null
    ? null
    : (existingApp.installSource ?? /* agent-created label */),
```

(the `unpackedLoadReplaceNote` copy needs a third source variant, e.g. "created by the agent"). A test where the existing app has no install record would pin it.

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a whitespace-padded manifest id is validated trimmed but installed untrimmed**

`WidgetPayloadValidation.id` returns the **raw** `manifest['id']` (untrimmed), while `_checkSchema` validates the **trimmed** form (`rawId.trim()` → `_checkId`) and `WidgetManifest.fromJson` also trims. So a manifest like:

```json
{"id": " fa-agents ", "name": "X", "version": "1.0.0"}
```

passes validation (the id rule `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` is enforced on the trimmed value), and then this line installs it into a **space-padded folder**:

```dart
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: id, // " fa-agents " — written as apps/ fa-agents /manifest.json
  ...
```

Verified locally: `inspection.id` = `" fa-agents "` and the env ends up with `apps/ fa-agents /` + a `.installed.json` key `" fa-agents "` — the stored id violates the very rule the validator just enforced. No traversal risk (regex rejects `/` and `..`), but the widget's stored id no longer matches the id rule, and the folder name carries whitespace everywhere (grid key, `open_app`, records).

Fix (one line, in `UnpackedWidgetLoader.install`):

```dart
final trimmed = id.trim();
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: trimmed,
  version: inspection.version ?? '0.0.0',
  files: inspection.files,
  origin: origin,
);
```

—or reject ids where `id != id.trim()` in the validator with a named `id_invalid` error. A regression test with a padded id belongs in `unpacked_loader_test.dart`.
"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the replace warning is skipped for agent-created apps — their code is overwritten silently**

The replace check keys off the install record:

```dart
final replaced = existing.where((app) => app.id == inspection.id).toList();
final existingApp = replaced.isEmpty ? null : replaced.first;
...
existingSource: existingApp?.installSource, // null for agent-created apps
```

and the dialog decides `final replaces = existingSource != null;`.

An **agent-created** app (built with Fa via file tools) has **no** `.installed.json` record, so `installSource` is `null` → `replaces` is `false` → the dialog renders as a plain fresh-load confirm ("Load" button, no warning banner), even though confirming **overwrites that app's code** (`installWidget` only protects files whose hashes are recorded — an agent-created app has none, so every file is replaced; only `storage.json` survives).

Ticket AC4 says "replacing an existing id asks for confirmation" — the load confirm still appears, but the explicit replace warning (naming what is being replaced) fires only when the old install came from the catalog or a previous unpacked load. The exact scenario gh-1616 enables — iterate on a widget with Fa, then load a worktree folder with the same id — silently replaces the agent-built code with only a generic confirm.

Fix: treat "an app with this id already exists" as the replace condition, and label the unknown source honestly, e.g.:

```dart
final replaces = existingApp != null;
...
existingSource: existingApp == null
    ? null
    : (existingApp.installSource ?? /* agent-created label */),
```

(the `unpackedLoadReplaceNote` copy needs a third source variant, e.g. "created by the agent"). A test where the existing app has no install record would pin it.

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a whitespace-padded manifest id is validated trimmed but installed untrimmed**

`WidgetPayloadValidation.id` returns the **raw** `manifest['id']` (untrimmed), while `_checkSchema` validates the **trimmed** form (`rawId.trim()` → `_checkId`) and `WidgetManifest.fromJson` also trims. So a manifest like:

```json
{"id": " fa-agents ", "name": "X", "version": "1.0.0"}
```

passes validation (the id rule `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` is enforced on the trimmed value), and then this line installs it into a **space-padded folder**:

```dart
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: id, // " fa-agents " — written as apps/ fa-agents /manifest.json
  ...
```

Verified locally: `inspection.id` = `" fa-agents "` and the env ends up with `apps/ fa-agents /` + a `.installed.json` key `" fa-agents "` — the stored id violates the very rule the validator just enforced. No traversal risk (regex rejects `/` and `..`), but the widget's stored id no longer matches the id rule, and the folder name carries whitespace everywhere (grid key, `open_app`, records).

Fix (one line, in `UnpackedWidgetLoader.install`):

```dart
final trimmed = id.trim();
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: trimmed,
  version: inspection.version ?? '0.0.0',
  files: inspection.files,
  origin: origin,
);
```

—or reject ids where `id != id.trim()` in the validator with a named `id_invalid` error. A regression test with a padded id belongs in `unpacked_loader_test.dart`.
"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the replace warning is skipped for agent-created apps — their code is overwritten silently**

The replace check keys off the install record:

```dart
final replaced = existing.where((app) => app.id == inspection.id).toList();
final existingApp = replaced.isEmpty ? null : replaced.first;
...
existingSource: existingApp?.installSource, // null for agent-created apps
```

and the dialog decides `final replaces = existingSource != null;`.

An **agent-created** app (built with Fa via file tools) has **no** `.installed.json` record, so `installSource` is `null` → `replaces` is `false` → the dialog renders as a plain fresh-load confirm ("Load" button, no warning banner), even though confirming **overwrites that app's code** (`installWidget` only protects files whose hashes are recorded — an agent-created app has none, so every file is replaced; only `storage.json` survives).

Ticket AC4 says "replacing an existing id asks for confirmation" — the load confirm still appears, but the explicit replace warning (naming what is being replaced) fires only when the old install came from the catalog or a previous unpacked load. The exact scenario gh-1616 enables — iterate on a widget with Fa, then load a worktree folder with the same id — silently replaces the agent-built code with only a generic confirm.

Fix: treat "an app with this id already exists" as the replace condition, and label the unknown source honestly, e.g.:

```dart
final replaces = existingApp != null;
...
existingSource: existingApp == null
    ? null
    : (existingApp.installSource ?? /* agent-created label */),
```

(the `unpackedLoadReplaceNote` copy needs a third source variant, e.g. "created by the agent"). A test where the existing app has no install record would pin it.

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. You are Fa, a coding agent (also called fa). Never refer to yourself as pi, Claude, or any other assistant name. You help with software engineering tasks in the working directory /home/runner/work/flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness. Use the read, write, ls, and bash tools to inspect and modify files and run commands. Be concise.

## Session recall — never answer about the past from assumption

1. **Reference = search.** When the user references any past decision, rule, task, or artifact ("remember when…", "the rules we made", "that issue from last week"), call `session_search` BEFORE answering. Never answer about the past from assumption.
2. **Resume ritual.** After a compaction boundary is crossed or the session resumes, read the obligations ledger block (the `<system-notice>` titled "obligations ledger") first; it is the contract of what is still owed.
3. **Commit in the open.** Before promising a follow-up, check the ledger. When you arm a timer or watch (`schedule_message`), state the reason clearly in the message text — the engine writes a `pending-wait` ledger entry from it, and the fired timer re-enters a context that knows why it exists.
4. **Durable ≠ session.** Cross-session rules go to long-term memory immediately (`memory_add`); session-scoped obligations stay in the ledger. Never misuse either layer for the other.
5. **Dig idioms.** Markers are the TOC. `session_search` locates, `compact_expand` reads. `read $FAH_SESSION_FILE:<line>` is the zero-tool fallback.

## FinalizeGate — verify produced state before declaring done

You are running unattended: nobody re-checks your work after you declare it. **Trivial turns — answer directly:** when the turn made NO tool calls at all — no files written or edited, no commands run, nothing created or changed; a pure question answered from what you already know — there is nothing to verify. Skip the checklist AND the task ledger entirely and reply plainly; the gate exists for produced state, and with none the checklist is noise.

The contract does NOT apply to turns like:

- **"почему ты баш команды вызываешь?"** — a "why did you…" question. Just answer it directly: no checklist, no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what does the `read` selector `:N` do?"** — a "what does X do" question. Just explain it: no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what's the status?"** — a status/explanation answer about work already done. Report it plainly: no re-verification, no ledger.

Those turns produced no state; running the checklist ritual on them is noise. Otherwise, before ANY final summary you MUST:

1. **Checklist** — re-quote every explicit requirement from the task text verbatim, one checklist item per requirement (files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints, outputs).
2. **Verify each item with a real command** against the produced state — never from memory, never "I wrote it earlier". Note expected vs actual.
3. **Fix or report every unmet item** — a failed item is either fixed and re-verified, or explicitly reported as unmet. Fix attempts are bounded: report, don't spiral.

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/.netrc`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed).
- **Grader parity** — your shell is not the verifier's: a produced entry point (a script/CLI the grader will run) is verified only when it survives the grader's own invocation. Re-run each produced entry point from a different working directory (`cd /` — any neutral cwd, never the session cwd) in a fresh subprocess with a clean env (no session-exported vars), capture stdout, stderr and exit code, and diff against the earlier in-session run. Any divergence — different output, files created via relative paths now missing, locale/encoding-dependent output — is a `fail` ledger item, not a pass.

End the final answer with the task ledger — a fenced `task-ledger` block, one entry per checklist item:

```task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  command: <the verification command you ran>
  expected: <what it should show>
  actual: <what it actually showed>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

`pass` = verified against the produced state; `fixed` = failed, then fixed and re-verified; `fail` = could not meet it, reported. A final answer whose ledger still has `fail` items without an explicit report is a protocol violation.

## Agent messaging

You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a13cb1-e0ca-7de4-bfa1-ec82dbd743ac/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — their orchestrators are reachable at `<theirSessionId>/main`, your subagents at their plain ids. Live instances also expose their session display name (`--session goal_builder`): `agent_directory` shows it next to the mailbox id, and `agent_message` accepts the name directly — `goal_builder` or `goal_builder/main` — so you rarely need the raw id. Use the `agent_directory` tool to list the live mailboxes (plus anything holding pending mail; pass `all: true` for long-dead ones and full mailbox ids — the default view truncates ids to save tokens) and `agent_message` to send. Each row also shows the last-activity time: `active 2m ago` means the watcher is live, `last active 3h ago (asleep)` means the process is gone. If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. Incoming mail is delivered to you automatically between turns (and wakes you when idle); reply with `agent_message` to the sender's address when a response is expected. Never guess mailbox addresses — read them from `agent_directory`.
When a hub is configured, `agent_directory` also lists hub peers beyond this project's file inboxes (embedded hosts, other machines) with their id and name — message them with `agent_message` the same way; the hub delivers even while a peer is offline (it drains when the peer reconnects).

Peers on OTHER machines are addressed `name@machine` (use a machine name you were told, or one from the peer itself): `agent_message to: "goal_builder@renderbox"` routes through the A2A gateway when this host's config has an `a2a.servers.renderbox` entry — delivery is synchronous there, so an error means the mail did NOT land (retry or tell the user). Without that config entry the send fails with the exact hint of what to add.

## The owner talks to you only

The owner's messages always arrive in YOUR inbox — subagents and children are your internal machinery, never the owner's address. Decide per message: answer directly when you know, or route it to the child doing that work with `task_send` and tell the owner you did (e.g. «передал fix503»); when the child's result lands, report it back. While children run you may go idle — the waiting row names them, and completions and new mail wake you.
